Pieces of the films were heat treated by a modified version of the standard Inconel 725 aging treatment, as guided by the work by Bahena et al. using a GSL1100X tube furnace (MTI Corporation) at a constant temperature of 730 ◦C for 5 h under a vacuum pressure of 7 × 10−5 Pa. strain-induced boundary migration (SIBM) process, in which changes in stored energy throughout the film due to residual stresses causes the boundaries of low energy grains to migrate towards high energy regions, yielding low energy grains with the same crystallographic orientation as the parent grain
a nucleation-based recrystallization mechanism, in which low energy grains grow at the expense of high energy neighbors, leading to an abnormal recrystallization process and misoriented grains

the SIBM process will be dominate towards the free surface of the film, as it typically occurs at low-moderate stored energy conditions [69], thereby facilitating the formation of rafted structures and enlarged ALGs with the preferred orientation.
most of the ALGs are formed by nucleation based abnormal recrystallization, which yields smaller grains due to limited nucleation sites
